domain: consumer safety / food recall regulatory classification
prediction_question: For a recall report opened in FDA's food enforcement system, will FDA classify it Class I (versus Class II/III)?
prediction_time: At recall initiation / report creation: product description, recalling firm, reason for recall, distribution scope and quantity are known; the classification is assigned by FDA during the classification process afterwards (and 'status' ongoing/terminated is post-hoc).
target_definition: Recall classification (Class I / II / III per 21 CFR, FDA's documented classification process), binarized as Class I vs rest for a runner-compatible task.

sources.name: openFDA Food Enforcement API
sources.access: anonymous, no key, JSON; verified live 2026-10-19

license_evidence: Measured 2026-10-19: GET https://api.fda.gov/food/enforcement.json?limit=1 answers anonymously and its meta block carries terms=https://open.fda.gov/terms/ and license=https://open.fda.gov/license/ plus the disclaimer 'Do not rely on openFDA to make decisions regarding medical care... results are unvalidated.' openFDA data is US Government public domain per its license page; the disclaimer must be carried on any derived release.

observed_2026_10_19.sample_row_fields_observed: state, classification ('Class II' in the first row), plus the documented report fields (recall initiation date, product description, reason for recall, recalling firm, classification, status)

rejection_reason: Equivalent already exists in usable form, so per the standing novelty test this is a rejection, not a candidate. The exact task on the exact source is a published 2025 paper: 'Hazard-portfolio patterns in US food recall severity' (PMC13526789) uses 28,448 openFDA food enforcement records (2012-2025), target = the three-level severity classification (Class I 44.1% / Class II 50.1% / Class III 5.8%), ML triage models with a firm-history baseline capturing 92% of the best model's performance, and explicit ML-assisted-triage conclusions. Supporting prior art: RecallRisk-BERT (arXiv 2606.27174) does the same severity-triage task on openFDA *device* recalls (54,165 records, 2002-2025); a Kaggle dataset ships an analysis-ready unified snapshot of FDA food/drug/device recalls with harmonised fields and parsed dates; SafeBite (OpenReview) fine-tunes classifiers to assign health-hazard evaluations from recall texts. What exists: the source, the task, the label distribution, models and baselines. What would be ours: only re-partitioning - a mirror, not a contribution.
next_action: None - dropped on novelty (2026-10-19). Do not reopen for classification triage from initiation-time fields. If a need ever arises in this family, it must be a different task (e.g. predicting *termination lag* rather than class) - a new candidate with its own novelty search.
